what: Turns the California AB-32 cap-and-trade programme on or off. When on, a carbon allowance price is added to Pacific census division (division 9) delivered fuel prices for residential, commercial and transportation (from 2015) and to California industrial prices; California efficiency rebates are doubled in the commercial technology cost logic for division 9; the refinery model gets a California AB32 constraint and allowance cost; the electricity dispatch code maps California commercial efficiency savings and costs into the electricity region; EPM keeps its California cap inputs. In cb2026 the value is 1, so it is on.

values.meaning: AB-32 on: allowance price in division 9 fuel prices (util_copyadjusted.f90:696) and industrial prices (ind.f), commercial division 9 rebates doubled (comm.f:1911, 1937), AB32 constraint and allowance cost in the refinery model (lfmodel.gms:1171), California EE savings and costs mapped in the electricity code (uefd.f:1392, 1535), EPM keeps cap inputs from its data file (epm_read.py:618)
AB-32 off: none of the above; EPM sets the cap to 272.727, and offset, cost containment, reserve and auction prices to 0 (epm_read.py:618-624)

allowed: 0 or 1 (code tests ==1 in most places and >0 in uefd.f; description says 0=Off, 1=On)
notes: RTOVALUE default differs by file: 0 in comm.f and uaimms.f, 1 in ind.f, uefd.f, tran.f, refine*.f and util_copyadjusted.f90; EPM defaults to '1'. Moot while the key is present in MOREOPT (cb2026 sets 1). Refinery gets it through a GDX element (refine.f:1816 writes it, lfprep.gms:3713 loads it, lfmodel.gms makes the AB32 constraint and allowance cost conditional on it). util_copyadjusted adds the allowance cost to division 9 prices from 2015 and only when ab_allow_p is above 0. The commercial doubling and price adders use census division 9 (Pacific), not only California. In uefd.f the California efficiency mapping applies only when CO2_STDSW is 0 or before CO2_STDY1 (uefd.f:1535). The AIMMS EFD model declares AB32SW (efd.ams:298) and uaimms.f writes ed::AB32SW, but no AIMMS code uses the parameter, so the EFD optimiser itself does not read it. tran.f:1247 sets TRANAB32 but nothing else uses it, so Transportation is affected only through the delivered prices. resd.f has only a comment about it; Residential is affected only through prices.
correction: models/efd/MainProject/efd.ams:298 is the only AB32SW hit in models/efd and models/ecp (declaration only), so 'CA cap in electricity' was overstated; the 'Oil and gas supply' tag has no AB32SW reader and tran.f:1247 TRANAB32 is unused.

what: Calendar year of the last year of the AEO projection. Several modules use it to size their projection horizon and expectation windows (commercial last year index, macro EViews sample end, refinery period set-up in refine.f, price and quantity expectations in NXPECT, coal expectations, and the last year of the NGPL price table). The GAMS refinery model has its own hard-coded 2050 and does not follow the key.

values.meaning: projection runs to 2050 (value in the CB2026 case)

allowed: a calendar year; model year arrays are fixed at 61 years (1990-2050, MNUMYR in includes/parametr:16), so values above 2050 are not supported
notes: Most Fortran reads default to 0 if the key is missing (comm.f, mac.f, refine.f, util_tools.f90:600), which would break year arithmetic; only coal_expect defaults to 2050. The 2050 ceiling comes from the array dimension MNUMYR=61 (includes/parametr:16); the comment at mnfactorx_parser.py:65 is about LASTYR. mac.f also writes the year into the EViews program (mamlastyr, mac.f:1734). The GAMS refinery model keeps its own AEOLSTYR scalar fixed at 2050 (lf_nem.gms:71), so a change to this key does not reach it. NXPECT uses it to extend expectation years past the AEO last year (up to MNXYR=91).
correction: The entry omits two things. The GAMS refinery model also uses AEOLSTYR (24 uses in models/lfmm/source/lfprep.gms, for example lfprep.gms:1403, 2089, 3806), but lf_nem.gms:71 declares it with a hard-coded default /2050/ and no NEMS code passes the key to it (refine.f only reads it locally at 1364), so changing the key does not move the GAMS horizon. And NGPL_STAT_PRICE (util_ngpl_stat_price.f90:100) uses it as the last year of the table feeding the ethane and propane pricing program when RUNRNGPL=1 (prenems.py:431-437; 1 in cb2026). Also the 2050 ceiling evidence at mnfactorx_parser.py:65 is a comment about LASTYR, not AEOLSTYR; the real limit is MNUMYR=61 (includes/parametr:16).

what: Turns on extra debug and validation output from the electricity capacity planning (ECP) interface to AIMMS, including the detailed ECPcoeff text files. Off saves run time.

values.meaning: write extra ECP coefficient debug files and AIMMS validation files
omit that extra output

notes: Code default is 1 if the key is missing; cb2026 sets 0. Passed to AIMMS as ec::AIMECPBG (uaimms.f:9583). Intended not to change results, but it also switches which coefficient-building path runs: at 1 the Fortran ecp_fill_aimms_coeff always runs (uecp.f:214) and AIMMS recomputes all coefficients (ecp.ams:290); at 0 the Fortran DVAL skips adding coefficients (uecp.f:32252). Whether the paths give identical results in cb2026 is unknown; it depends on ECPARRAYS_ALL statuses.
correction: It is not only a debug-output switch. At 1 the Fortran ECP coefficient fill always runs (uecp.f:214) and ecp.ams:290 runs every AIMMS coefficient calculation even when Fortran coefficients are passed; at 0, uecp.f:32252 sets iskip=1 so the Fortran DVAL does not add coefficients. Which path is live in cb2026 depends on the ECPARRAYS_ALL file statuses read in uaimms.f:2608 (CheckToDisableECPOMLLP).

values.meaning: write extra EFD coefficient debug files and AIMMS validation files
omit that extra output

notes: Code default is 1 if missing; cb2026 sets 0. Passed to AIMMS as ed::AIMEFDBG (uaimms.f:132). Intended not to change results. Besides debug files, it controls whether the Fortran EFD LP coefficients are built (uefd.f:6961, 6967); with 0 they are skipped only if USE_AIMEFD_SLNADJ is true and SKIP_EFDOML is true (set from the EFDARRAYS_ALL file, uaimms.f:2565-2577). DVAL sets AIMEFDBG=1 at uefd.f:7092 whenever it is called. Whether the skip happens in cb2026 is unknown.
correction: It also gates Fortran LP generation: REVEFD and efd_fill_aimms_coeff run when AIMEFDBG=1 or USE_AIMEFD_SLNADJ is false or SKIP_EFDOML is false (uefd.f:6961, 6967); with 0 and both flags otherwise they are skipped. Also DVAL overwrites AIMEFDBG=1 (uefd.f:7092), so once REVEFD runs the key's 0 is overridden for the rest of that call.

what: Discount rate (required rate of return) for greenhouse gas allowance banking, entered in permille (74 means 7.4 percent a year). In an emissions policy case, EPM uses it in two places: the allowance price path grows at this rate during the banking period (epm_core.py:339), and with permit or market flags on and no banking it discounts the price backward from the start year to the price year (epm_core.py:149, 188-206). In cb2026 all EPM policy flags are 0, so it has no effect.

values.meaning: 7.4 percent per year (code divides the value by 10 to get percent)

notes: Applies only when an emissions tax, permit or market flag is on (epm_control.toml sets tax_flag, permit_flag, market_flag and bank_flag all to 0 in lines 18-29, so it is inert in cb2026). The permit or market without bank branch (epm_core.py:188-206) uses it too, so banking is not required. Python default is 74 if the key is missing. Fortran does not read it.
correction: epm_core.py:149 and 188-206 use r also when bank_flag is 0 (permit or market only), contradicting 'only matters when banking is in use'; epm_control.toml:18-29 shows every flag is 0, so it is inert in cb2026.

what: Calendar year in which allowance banking and the associated price path start applying inside a cap-and-trade period in the emissions module (EPM). Only matters when a carbon policy with banking is switched on. In cb2026 all EPM policy flags are 0, so it has no effect.
notes: Python default is 2051 if the key is missing. The code clamps it: if below bank_startyr in the EPM control file it is raised to bank_startyr, and if above bank_endyr it is reset to bank_startyr (not to bank_endyr). The shipped models/epm/input/epm_control.toml has bank_startyr=2012 and bank_endyr=2040, so the cb2026 value 2051 is reset to 2012. Used in epm_core.py:233, 472, 509, 517 and epm_regula_falsi.py:327. Has no effect unless bank_flag and one of tax_flag, permit_flag or market_flag are on (epm_core.py:469-472); epm_control.toml sets tax_flag, permit_flag, market_flag and bank_flag all to 0 (lines 18-29), so the key is inert in cb2026.
correction: epm_control.toml:32 sets bank_endyr = 2040 (old notes said the end was 2050) and lines 18-29 set every policy flag to 0, so BANKONYR is inert in cb2026, which was not stated.

what: Baseline residential and commercial electricity consumption (billion kWh by census division and year) from an unbenchmarked NEMS run, read by both Residential (BLDBASEREAD) and Commercial (COMServiceDemand). notes: The 111d rule it was built for is repealed and EPA111D is 0 in cb2026, but CALC111D still runs: comm.f:824 calls it unconditionally and resd.f:588 calls it in the RECS-year block. The savings feed the California AB32 efficiency credit in uefd.f:1534-1541, which applies when AB32SW>0 (1 in cb2026) and no CO2 standard is in force. Years before 2017 are zeroed (comm.f:11132, resd.f:14976). The FILELIST row is owned by EXR, so it is dropped when Residential is off, which would also break the Commercial open at comm.f:2196.
correction: what only repeats the scedes description and modules omits Commercial, which also opens the file (comm.f:2196). Nothing says the baseline matters in cb2026 through the California AB32 path while EPA111D is 0.

what: Benchmark year for price and quantity expectations. Expectation variables equal actual values up to this year, and extrapolation or myopia starts the year after. In practice it has no effect on a forecast run.

allowed: a calendar year (values above 1989 are converted to an index by subtracting 1989) or a year index
notes: The only use is IDXSY = MAX(CURIYR-1, BMYREXP). With BMYREXP at index 7 (1996) and forecast years in the 2020s, CURIYR-1 always wins, so the value never binds. It would only matter for a benchmark year later than the current model year. The variable is saved after first read (initialized to 0), so it is read once per run. what: Upper cap on the annual growth rate NEMS assumes when it extrapolates future electricity demand series (the first five quantity vectors) for its expectation variables. notes: ELGREXP = 1 + value/10/100. It is applied only to the first five expectation quantity vectors (IV <= 5: XQELRS, ELCM, ELTR, ELIN, ELAS, the electricity demand series), via GDEM = MIN(GDEM, ELGREXP) (util_tools.f90:700). Because GDEM is already capped at 1.05 on line 698, the base value 50 does not bind; any lower value tightens the cap. Further, cb2026 sets EUEDEXP=1 (scedes.cb2026.csv:118), and util_tools.f90:728-741 then overwrites GDEM for IV 1 to 5 with the ratio of actual restart-file demand (QELRS, QELCM, QELTR, QELIN, QELAS), so the ELGREXP-capped rate is not used in cb2026. The XQEL* arrays are read by uldsm.f (for example lines 419-449). Identical code in source/util_tools_prepro.f90:566.
correction: util_tools.f90:728-741 under EUEDEXP.EQ.1 (cb2026 value 1) replaces the capped GDEM for IV 1-5, so ELGREXP is inert in cb2026; old text said planning is 'built against these capped growth rates' and 'I did not trace which modules consume'.

Turns on the analysis of EPA's Clean Power Plan (Section 111(d)): national utility energy efficiency subsidies are subtracted from residential and commercial equipment, shell and lighting costs, 111(d) costs are tracked, and the macro model gets mac111d=1 and runs its 111(d) branches. In cb2026 the value is 0, so this is off, except that the commercial cost code still subtracts the 111(d) subsidy for census division 9 when AB32SW=1.

values.meaning: 111(d) on: subsidies subtracted from residential and commercial equipment, shell and lighting costs (resd.f:898, comm.f:1914), CALC111D run in commercial (comm.f:817), residential COST111RES accumulates (resd.f:15004), macro mac111d=1 (mac.f:2505) and sub_mac111d plus six mac111d branches in mcevcode.txt
111(d) off: residential 111(d) subsidy terms multiplied by zero, CALC111D not run, mac111d=0. Exception: commercial division 9 keeps the 111(d) subsidy when AB32SW=1 (comm.f:1919-1921)

allowed: 0 or 1 (commercial code tests ==1; residential uses it as a 0/1 multiplier via FLOAT(EPA111D))
notes: Default 0 everywhere; cb2026 value 0. Residential subsidy terms are multiplied by FLOAT(EPA111D), so a value other than 0 or 1 would scale them, but only 0 and 1 are meaningful. Commercial CALC111D runs only if exactly 1. In the commercial technology cost logic (comm.f:1911-1950) the division 9 branch subtracts the 111(d) subsidy whenever AB32SW=1, even with EPA111D=0. The electricity module does not read the key directly. Macro branches on mac111d are at mcevcode.txt lines 70, 272, 461, 520, 737 and 1141.
correction: Old what said subsidies were 'added to' costs; comm.f:1914 and resd.f:898 subtract them. comm.f:1919-1921 also shows the AB32SW exception that makes EPA111D=0 not fully off in cb2026; old notes ended with 'I did not check macro effects'.

off

what: Path to ephrts.f90, the Fortran source of the electricity hydrogen submodule (EPHRTS: hydrogen made by electrolysis, with prices and quantities passed to the capacity planning model). One of the files compiled into the pyfiler1 extension.

notes: Every normal setup runs the build step: nems_submit.py:148-151 calls make_pyd_files unless PREPRO is yes, and flags 0, 1 and 2 all reach the meson step (meson_exec.py:76). That step rewrites meson.build from this key when the text differs (meson_exec.py:205-211), then runs meson setup and compile (meson_exec.py:84, 88). So a changed path is compiled on the next submit. Selects which source file is compiled, not whether EPHRTS runs; the run-time switch is the separate key EPHRTS (nems_setup.py:154, nexec.py:166), which is 0 in cb2026 (scedes.cb2026.csv:116), so the compiled EPHRTS routines are not run in cb2026.

Chooses how future end-use electricity demand growth is expected in NXPECT (the expectation variables XQ for electricity sales to residential, commercial, transportation, industrial and all sectors). With 1, expected growth for each future year is the year-on-year growth of the electricity sales already in the restart file (perfect foresight) up to the last year of the AEO projection period (AEOLSTYR, 2050 in cb2026), then held at the last growth rate. With 0, the growth rate is computed from past sales growth.

values.meaning: perfect foresight: for each future year up to AEOLSTYR, expected growth = QELxx(year)/QELxx(year-1) from the restart file; after AEOLSTYR, held at the AEOLSTYR growth rate

expected growth is the trailing-average growth of electricity sales over the last NYRS years (starting no earlier than LAST_STEO_YR), capped at 1.05 and at the ELGREXP multiplier, or DEM_GRW when the EXE/GRW_XYR option applies

notes: Applies to expectation vectors IV 1 to 5 in NXPECT (QELRS, QELCM, QELTR, QELIN, QELAS). Code default is 0; cb2026 sets 1 with AEOLSTYR=2050 and ELGREXP=50. With 1, the ELGREXP cap and the DEM_GRW override are bypassed for all years after the start year because GDEM is reassigned at util_tools.f90:728-741. Same code in util_tools_prepro.f90:679. NXPECT runs on iteration 1 only (nems_iteration_loop.py:93).
correction: 'up to the last actual year' is false. The switch point is AYR = AEOLSTYR - 1989 (util_tools.f90:600-601), the last year of the AEO projection period (2050 in cb2026), not the last historical year. With 1, expected growth for the five electricity demand vectors follows next-cycle-style restart sales growth for every year through 2050, then holds the 2050 growth rate to the end of the expectation horizon. The 0 case was left untraced but is readable: growth over the trailing NYRS years capped at 1.05 and at ELGREXP (cb2026 ELGREXP=50, so 1.05), unless the EXE/GRW_XYR block replaces it with DEM_GRW (util_tools.f90:696-725). Modules Residential, Commercial, Industrial and Transportation are not established; they only supply the QEL* quantities.

what: Turns the hydrogen module (HMM) on or off for the run. HMM is not run; the model loop skips it

what: Exponent (value/100) on cumulative production in the expected natural gas price curve once the price has reached the unconventional-gas level (EXPNGIPT). In cb2026 it only shapes expected gas prices after 2050, because WELLPF = 1 replaces the curve with perfect-foresight prices through 2050.

values.meaning: exponent 1.3
exponent 1.5; Fortran default if the key is missing

notes: Applied when last year's wellhead price is at or above UPF (EXPNGIPT) (util_tools.f90:1041-1042) or when an expected price crosses UPF (lines 1077-1079); the curve is then refitted with this exponent (EXNGINVERT, line 1161). EXNGUTIL is called by NXPECT only when I4SCNT equals 2 (util_tools.f90:915-916; cb2026 sets I4SCNT = 2, scedes.cb2026.csv:123). cb2026 gate: WELLPF = 1 (scedes.cb2026.csv:146), so EXNGUTIL fits the curve only once per process (ONCEPF, util_tools.f90:1065 and 1102), overwrites XOGWPRNG for every year through LASTYR (2050) with the smoothed perfect-foresight price (lines 1089-1094), and uses the fitted curve only for 2051 to 2080, as the ratio WHDRTE(IY)/WHDRTE(LASTYR) applied to the 2050 price (line 1098). The electricity capacity planner looks UNFPH = 30 years ahead (input/emm/emmcntl.txt:2395), so from model year 2022 on it sees those post-2050 prices (uecp.f:6264-6266). XOGWPRNG is read by the electricity capacity planner (uecp.f:6258 and 6266 in the UPCRVSW = 2 branch that cb2026 uses; 6235 and 6244 in the other branch; models/ecp/MainProject/ecp.ams:25110); a grep of source, includes and models finds no other reader. Same code in util_tools_prepro.f90:937.

The industrial Fortran also reads it directly (RTOVALUE) so the cement routine calls cementCCS only when it is 1; that read does not depend on which partition runs.

A module is only run if it is also in the run-type list (user.jogpar), and the run order comes from the ORDx keys. what: First execution year, stored as a year index (value minus 1990 plus 1). Modules use it as the 'first forecast year' marker, for example to run one-time initialisation in the first year of the first iteration.

allowed: calendar year; the code converts it as FIRSYR-1990+1
notes: The main year loop always starts at index 1 (nems_flow.py:134, range(1, LASTYR+1)), so the iteration loop does not skip years. Many one-time initialisation tests (CURIYR .EQ. FIRSYR) in mac.f, world.f, util.f, uecp.f, udat.f and EPM would also shift. Left at 1990 in cb2026.
correction: Notes say changing FIRSYR only moves 'first year' tests. That is false: models/main/postnems.py:49 loops range(FIRSYR, LASTYR+1) for the end-of-run sums, source/comm.f:534 makes the commercial module return early when FIRSYR is later than its first year, and the reporter builds its year range from it (RW_reporter_main.py:417, 2873). EPM also tests it (epm_core.py:173).

what: Foresight option for the model's expectation variables. In NXPECT: 1 (myopic) sets the price growth window to zero years, so GROWTH returns 0 and expected prices are held flat at the start-year value; 2 (adaptive) extrapolates prices at the trailing growth rate over NYRS years (capped 0 to 5 percent a year); 3 (perfect) sets the start index to the current year and the end index to the current year (unless it is the last year), so no extrapolation is applied. In the electricity module (util.f), at 3 the expectation and planning setup runs every iteration instead of iteration 1 only, and the gas-use expectation scaling is skipped.

values.meaning: myopic: NXPECT price growth window is zero years (IDXGY_P=IDXSY), so expected prices stay flat at the start-year value; electricity expectations set on iteration 1 only
adaptive: NXPECT extrapolates prices at the trailing NYRS-year growth rate, capped at 1.05; electricity expectations set on iteration 1 only
perfect: NXPECT start and end index are the current year (extrapolation loops are empty); electricity expectations refreshed every iteration; gas consumption expectation scaling skipped

allowed: 1, 2 or 3; all three behave differently in NXPECT
notes: Readers: util_tools.f90:624, 627, 633 (NXPECT) and util_tools_prepro.f90:575-584; util.f:562, 914, 2875. Quantity growth windows (IDXGY_Q) are not changed by value 1. NXPECT itself runs on iteration 1 only (nems_iteration_loop.py:93). cb2026 uses 2.
correction: Two claims are false: 'Only util.f reads it' and 'Code does not distinguish 1 from 2'. NXPECT (util_tools.f90:624-633) sets IDXGY_P=IDXSY for I4SITE=1 (zero-year price growth window), and for 3 sets the start and end index to the current year. NXPECT sets expectations for all prices and quantities, not just electricity.

what: Position of the coal module (CMM) in the order NEMS runs its modules each model year. Modules run in ascending order of this number; the module runs at all only if its EXC switch is 1 and it is allowed in the run type.

allowed: integer (parsed with int()); only the ranking between modules matters. Ties are not rejected in code
notes: set_nems_modules builds {module: int(value)} from every scedes key starting with ORD, sorts by value, keeps modules whose EX switch is 1 and that appear in the run-type list (jogpar, prenems.py:46-49), and nems_flow.py loops over that list inside every year. Order changes which module sees which module's latest results, so it can change convergence and results, not just timing. Any scedes key starting with ORD must map to a letter in module_map or the run fails with a KeyError. A module with no ORD key would not run even if EX is 1.

Sets the weight on the stored previous wellhead price when smoothing the perfect-foresight expected natural gas price against the price in the restart file, for each year from the first model year to LASTYR. Higher means the stored previous price counts for more and expectations move more slowly.

values.meaning: new value is a 50/50 average of the restart price and the stored previous price

notes: Only used when WELLPF = 1 (cb2026 sets 1). Formula (util_tools.f90:1014): new = restart price x (1 - w) + stored previous price x w, where the stored price is XOGWPRNGPF(2,...). If that stored price is zero or negative, line 1010 sets it to the restart price and the weight then changes nothing. XOGWPRNGPF is part of the restart commons (includes/mxpblk:37); the code does not show whether the restart in use holds a positive stored price. The block sits in the CURIYR == FIRSYR, CURITR == 1, .NOT. ONCE section of EXNGUTIL, and ONCE is a saved flag, so it runs once per process, not once per cycle. The smoothed result becomes XOGWPRNG through LASTYR (lines 1089-1094), which the electricity capacity planner reads (uecp.f:6258, 6266). Same code in util_tools_prepro.f90:939.
correction: Old entry missed that the weight does nothing when the restart holds no prior stored price (util_tools.f90:1010) and listed Oil and gas supply, which is not shown to be affected (OGWPRNG is an NGTDM output, includes/ngtdmrep:14).

what: Path to the Fortran source of the refinery module that gets compiled into the model. The default refine.f, refine_hogs.f (highogs case) and refine_logs.f (lowogs case) differ in how they set WTI_PRICE after the last historical year. WTI_PRICE then feeds industrial chemical product prices (ind.f:3802), the expected oil price in util_tools.f90, NGPL pricing (util_ngpl_stat_price.f90:118) and report tables.

values.meaning: WTI_PRICE after the last historical year is 0.98 * weight * last historical WTI + (1 - weight) * model crude price RFCRUDEWHP(2,1); the history weight starts at about 10 percent (times 0.98) and falls linearly to 0 by 2050 (refine.f:296-306)

WTI_PRICE is set directly to the model crude price RFCRUDEWHP(2,1) in every year the refinery model runs (2010 on); the guard 'curiyr+1989 .gt. HISTLYR' compares a calendar year with an index so it never blocks (refine_logs.f:286)

No history weight (WTIDECLINE is 0). WTI_PRICE equals the model crude price until HISTLYR+1989+12, then (1 + 2049/(2500*(2050-(HISTLYR+1990)))) times the model price through 2050, a constant markup of roughly 3 to 4 percent for a last historical year near 2025 (refine_hogs.f:296-306)

allowed: a path to a Fortran source file; the repo ships refine.f, refine_hogs.f, refine_logs.f
notes: Only the WTI_PRICE block differs in substance between the three files (the rest of the diff is whitespace). The highogs and lowogs case files point here, so it works as a scenario lever by file swap. Changing the value only matters when the code is rebuilt (meson step runs for FULL_BUILD_FLAG 0, 1 or 2, scripts/setup/src/meson_exec.py:76); a run that reuses an existing build ignores it. HISTLYR is an index set outside these files; the markup size in refine_hogs.f depends on it.
correction: refine_hogs.f:302 gives WTIADJFACT = -(slope+intercept)/2500 which is about -0.034, not near zero, so WTI_PRICE is about 3 percent above the model price, not 'essentially equal'; refine_logs.f:286 compares a calendar year with an index so it overwrites in all refinery years; downstream use now traced (ind.f:3802, util_tools.f90:904, util_ngpl_stat_price.f90:118).

what: When above 0, the refinery model (LFMM) subtracts a 'rent' for unused refinery capacity from the domestic crude wellhead price it reports (LFMMOUT_RFCRUDEWHP). When NCNTRL_CURCALYR > 2020, lfreport.gms:3613-3625 sets the rent to 15 (2013 dollars) minus the gap between the foreign supply curve marginal price and the domestic crude balance marginal price (L_Sweet, region 2 used for all crudes), capped at 6.90 (1.00 for condensate); it can go negative. The reported price RFCRUDEWHP feeds the oil supply model (models/hsm/module_unf.py:1023) and the WTI price in refine.f:306.
correction: Old what said the rent is added to domestic crude prices; lfreport.gms:3632 subtracts CrudeWHP_rent from LFMMOUT_RFCRUDEWHP, and the 2020+ adjustment (lfreport.gms:3613-3625) is now traced.

Master switch for benchmarking to the Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) in the early forecast years. When on, residential and commercial results are benchmarked to STEO and then phased out, and natural gas end-use prices and Canadian exports are aligned to STEO. Transportation is different: only residual fuel is scaled to STEO growth, and the gap between STEO and TDM gasoline, diesel and jet fuel goes into balance-sector rows while TDM's own use of those fuels is unchanged. When off, those modules skip STEO benchmarking.

STEO benchmarking off

allowed: 0 or 1; code tests ==1 (residential tests ==0 for off)
notes: Commercial also needs ComSTEOBM=1 from its KPARM input (comm.f:726, 9137; kparm.txt sets it to 1). Natural gas also needs STEONG=1 (nems_ngmm.ams:1877, 1908, 9163). Industrial declares the variable (ind.f:2836) but has no use of it. Residential off-switch sets the last STEO year to the last history year plus one (resd.f:13714). Transportation uses the switch only in TBENCHMARK (tran.f:8883, 8994). The AIMMS parameter text says 1=on, 2=off (nems_ngmm.ams:12070), but the code tests =1.
correction: what says transportation results are pulled toward STEO values. In tran.f only residual fuel is scaled to STEO growth (tran.f:8883-8887); for gasoline, diesel and jet fuel the gap between STEO and TDM is put into the balance-sector rows QMGBS, QDSBS and QJFBS (tran.f:8994-9006), and TDM's own consumption is not moved toward STEO. With STEOBM 0 the balance sector holds its MER-year share (tran.f:9007-9009).

what: Names the file RFM_WDUMP.txt that Renewables writes. Scedes description: renewable output file.

Switches how electric utilities expect natural gas wellhead prices to evolve in their capacity planning. 1 uses 'perfect foresight': the expected price path is a smoothed blend of the previous cycle's guess and the actual wellhead price from the restart file. 0 uses an adaptive expectation extrapolated from a supply curve and an assumed production growth rate.

values.meaning: perfect foresight: for expectation years up to the last forecast year, the expected wellhead price is PFGUESS percent (scedes 50) times the previous guess plus the rest times the wellhead price from the restart file; years after the last forecast year grow with the adaptive path's year-to-year ratio
adaptive expectations from a supply curve with assumed production growth, recomputed on every call

allowed: 0 or 1; code only tests for 1 and 0
notes: Read via RTOVALUE with default 0 in EXNGUTIL, only on the first iteration of the first year. EXNGUTIL is called from NXPECT only when I4SCNT=2 (util_tools.f90:915); cb2026 sets I4SCNT=2. With WELLPF=1 the expectation loop runs once per run (guard ONCEPF, util_tools.f90:1065 and 1110), so the expected path is fixed after the first pass; with 0 it is recomputed every call. util_tools_prepro.f90 is a duplicate copy (line 938). The expected price XOGWPRNG is consumed by the electric capacity planner (uecp.f:6235, also AIMMS ecp.ams:25110). PFGUESS is the weight on the previous guess, not on the restart price. Natural gas was removed from modules because no natural gas module code reads XOGWPRNG or WELLPF.
correction: util_tools.f90:1006 weights the previous guess by WHATWGTPF (PFGUESS) and the restart price by 1 minus that; the old meaning read as if PFGUESS weighted the restart price. Natural gas was listed with no reader (XOGWPRNG is only used in uecp.f and ecp.ams).

what: Scales how fast hydrogen electrolyzer capital costs fall relative to the Reference case (zero carbon technology cost cases). 1 keeps Reference behavior with normal endogenous learning. 0 freezes electrolyzer capital costs at their 2026 level (ZTCBasisYear) from 2026 on. A fraction between 0 and 1, or a whole number above 1 (read as a percent), gives a straight-line cut below the Reference capital costs, reaching that fraction in the last model year, starting from 2026.

values.meaning: Reference: capital costs and learning run as normal; the final model year's capital costs are written to CapitalCostsByYearReference.txt for the low case to read
electrolyzer capital costs held at the 2026 value (ZTCBasisYear) for all later years (code comment calls it the High ZTC case)
value above 1 is divided by 100, so 0.40: electrolyzer capital costs are cut linearly from 2026 to 40% below the Reference costs in the last model year (the Low ZTC case)

allowed: 0, a fraction between 0 and 1, 1, or a whole-number percent above 1 (divided by 100)
notes: Through this key the only consumer is the hydrogen model (HMM), via h2_runval.txt. Only electrolyzer technologies (prodTech_elec) are changed. ZTCBasisYear is 2026 (models/hmm/input/h2config.txt:27). The low case reads the Reference capital cost file (models/hmm/data/CapitalCostsByYearReference.txt) at first-year setup (nems_hmm.ams:376), so it needs a Reference run's output to exist. Other modules' ZTC cases are driven by separate input files chosen by side case, not by this key, for example wgeparm_lowztc.txt, whydro_lowztc.txt, rsgentk_lowztc.txt. The description says '1 = no exogenous learning', but the code says 1 means learning runs as normal; trust the code. Sending 100 gives 1.0 after division and behaves like Reference. The high/low labels follow the side-case names: highztc sets 0, lowztc sets 40. nems_hmm.ams:333 hard-codes ZTCCOSTM := 1.0 only in a standalone-AIMMS branch. Active in cb2026 because EXH=1; the cb2026 value 1 is the Reference setting.
correction: S6 Output.ams:741-742 holds costs at CapitalCostsByYear(ZTCBasisYear), and h2config.txt:27 sets ZTCBasisYear to 2026, not 'first year'; the reduction ramp (S6 Output.ams:138) also starts at ZTCBasisYear.
